nodes.label: Technical Guidelines for SSF Data Harmonization in the WIO Region
nodes.norm_label: technical guidelines for ssf data harmonization in the wio region

nodes.label: Integrated Data Harmonization Framework (IDHF)
nodes.rationale: Organizes harmonization into three interconnected phases (Diagnostic Assessment; Design and Standardization; Implementation and Sustainability) so guidelines can be operationalized into actionable technical specifications.

nodes.label: Minimum Common Denominator
nodes.rationale: A core set of consistently-defined variables every institution must provide, enabling cross-dataset comparison without forcing all organizations onto one identical form; it represents the intersection of what all institutions can feasibly contribute while preserving flexibility to collect extra variables.

nodes.label: Participatory Diagnostic Survey of Data Collection Practices
nodes.rationale: Maps what entities currently measure, how they define variables, and which tools/formats they use BEFORE prescribing a fixed minimum set, so the framework is grounded in operational realities rather than imposed top-down.
nodes.norm_label: participatory diagnostic survey of data collection practices

nodes.label: Regional Scoping Assessment (26 institutions, 10 WIO countries)
nodes.rationale: Found catch/effort captured by 88%, vessel/gear by 84%, socio-economic by only 48%; 88% use consistent internal standards but only 28% externally compatible; financial sustainability the top barrier (68%); 81.8% support open access. Confirms a solid data-collection foundation but a lack of coordination mechanisms.
nodes.norm_label: regional scoping assessment (26 institutions, 10 wio countries)

nodes.label: Data Collection Heterogeneity (five dimensions)
nodes.rationale: Heterogeneity spans five dimensions: information collected; paper vs. digital forms; terminology/variable definitions; species lists & taxonomic resolution; and fishery contextual information.

nodes.label: Terms/Variable Standardization
nodes.rationale: Different organizations use divergent labels for the same concept (Area vs Landing site vs Region; Monofilament Nets vs Gillnets; Linha de mao vs Handlines; Swahili vs English), so common definitions and ontology mappings are needed for collections to 'speak the same language'.

nodes.label: Species List & Taxonomic Resolution Heterogeneity
nodes.rationale: Organizations record species at species-level vs mixed (species/genus) resolution and under many local names (e.g., Sardina pilchardus = Pilchard / Sardine / Sardinha), resolved by FAO 3-alpha codes (PIL), shared photo guides, and enumerator training.

nodes.label: Functional Requirements for Electronic Data Collection Tools
nodes.rationale: Tool-agnostic requirements (offline capture, built-in validation, controlled picklists, GPS capture, open export formats, multilingual, open-source, API/middleware, photo capture) avoid mandating one platform while ensuring data quality and interoperability across the diversity of tools already in use.
nodes.norm_label: functional requirements for electronic data collection tools

nodes.label: Paper vs. Digital Data Collection
nodes.rationale: Paper entails manual transcription errors, weeks/months of delay, data stuck in local offices, and no real-time validation; digital allows direct device entry, immediate sync+backup, built-in validation, and automatic export into analysis pipelines. 88% of institutions already use digital platforms, signalling readiness for a coordinated transition.

nodes.label: Centralized Tool-Agnostic Data Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Accepts data from multiple collection platforms and applies standardized transformation, validation, and formatting before ingestion into a central/regional repository, so diverse tools can converge to a common standard at the aggregation level.

nodes.label: Standardized Sampling Methodologies
nodes.rationale: Standardizing variables alone is insufficient if sampling designs are incompatible; principles cover sampling frames, stratification, temporal/spatial coverage, raising procedures, and QA/QC so data from different institutions can be aggregated.

nodes.label: Raising / Scaling Procedures for Total Estimates
nodes.rationale: Fishery-level census data (active fishers, number of boats) provide denominators to raise sample-based catch/effort to population totals; standardized landing-site metadata with coordinates enables spatial aggregation.
nodes.norm_label: raising / scaling procedures for total estimates

nodes.label: Regional Data Dictionary
nodes.rationale: Co-created with SWIOFC and WGDS, it defines core variables, metadata, classification systems, and standardized terms (with AQFO URI mappings as a medium-term goal) so all institutions work from an aligned vocabulary; maintained as a living document.

nodes.label: Data Governance & Institutional Arrangements
nodes.rationale: Recommends legally binding data-sharing agreements (access levels, ownership, custodianship), and a regional data governance board potentially under SWIOFC, with national experts nominated by member countries linking regional governance to national implementation nodes.

nodes.label: Phased Implementation Roadmap (2026-2030)
nodes.rationale: Six phases: Diagnostic (Q4 2026-Q1 2027); Standardization (Q2-Q3 2027); Pilot testing in Kenya/Mozambique/Zanzibar (Q3 2027-Q2 2028); Evaluation (Q3 2028); Regional rollout to SWIOFC member states (Q4 2028-Q4 2029); Sustained operation (2030+) with sustainable financing.

nodes.label: Data-Information-Knowledge-Insight Integration
nodes.source_location: Slide: Individual datasets become more powerful when integrated
nodes.rationale: Individual datasets gain value when integrated: disconnected data points become information, then knowledge (linked), then insight (highlighted findings).

nodes.label: COASTS (Small Scale Fisheries Analysis Platform)
nodes.rationale: A multi-country fishing-effort/CPUE analysis platform shown alongside PESKAS Zanzibar; visualizes fishing activity grid cells and district comparisons across the WIO.

nodes.label: Five Levels of Digital Information Intervention (Control / Individual / Community / Individual+Community / Individual+Community+Neighbor)
nodes.rationale: The study tests increasingly localized/disaggregated digital feedback to find the trade-off in information focus that best promotes sustainable fishing behavior and governance.
